remaining_provider_connections.observer_scope: Instant wall time for sequential registry lock and per-connection observer collection; excludes final outer JSON serialization; not workload time

vfs.byte_scope: requested native xRead/xWrite bytes; confirmed only on SQLITE_OK; partial error bytes unavailable; xSync bytes are zero
vfs.checkpoint_scope: matched Instant wall time from CKPT_START arrival to CKPT_DONE arrival; backfill copy window only, after initial WAL sync and before final database truncate/sync; signals do not prove checkpoint success
vfs.lifecycle_scope: native file/context lifecycle including observer sidecar opens and closes; live gauges are never reset
vfs.scope: process selected observed native VFS invocations including external connections and connection close; excludes observer read/write/sync and checkpoint signals, SHM, mmap and other VFS operations; not syscalls or physical device IOPS

host_block_device.scope: one explicitly selected block device or driver, shared by all processes and kernel writeback; identity does not establish datastore/file/VM mapping; no summation or physical-flash attribution

process_disk.scope: OS accounting for one observer PID; character/syscall counters include cached and non-disk I/O; Linux write bytes are charged when dirtied and cancelled bytes remain separate; no child/container/remote-datastore or physical-flash attribution implied

os_io.sampling_window: boundary capture start to start; sequential observations, observer work included; no atomic multi-counter or API wall-time bound

resources.scope: one process includes clients, servers, verification and background; System Rust allocations exclude foreign C allocators; QUIC UDP bytes exclude IP/UDP headers; atomic allocator instrumentation affects throughput

terminal_cleanup.scope: server close and filesystem shutdown/drop; before fresh verification; includes process background and observer work; not checkpoint-only I/O

runtime.scope: observed Tokio scheduler worker pool size; not busy or physical thread count; per-client I/O depth and workload unchanged

remaining_provider_connections.observer_scope: Instant wall time for sequential registry lock and per-connection observer collection; excludes final outer JSON serialization; not workload time

vfs.byte_scope: requested native xRead/xWrite bytes; confirmed only on SQLITE_OK; partial error bytes unavailable; xSync bytes are zero
vfs.checkpoint_scope: matched Instant wall time from CKPT_START arrival to CKPT_DONE arrival; backfill copy window only, after initial WAL sync and before final database truncate/sync; signals do not prove checkpoint success
vfs.lifecycle_scope: native file/context lifecycle including observer sidecar opens and closes; live gauges are never reset
vfs.scope: process selected observed native VFS invocations including external connections and connection close; excludes observer read/write/sync and checkpoint signals, SHM, mmap and other VFS operations; not syscalls or physical device IOPS

host_block_device.scope: one explicitly selected block device or driver, shared by all processes and kernel writeback; identity does not establish datastore/file/VM mapping; no summation or physical-flash attribution

process_disk.scope: OS accounting for one observer PID; character/syscall counters include cached and non-disk I/O; Linux write bytes are charged when dirtied and cancelled bytes remain separate; no child/container/remote-datastore or physical-flash attribution implied

os_io.sampling_window: boundary capture start to start; sequential observations, observer work included; no atomic multi-counter or API wall-time bound

resources.scope: one process includes clients, servers, verification and background; System Rust allocations exclude foreign C allocators; QUIC UDP bytes exclude IP/UDP headers; atomic allocator instrumentation affects throughput

terminal_cleanup.scope: server close and filesystem shutdown/drop; before fresh verification; includes process background and observer work; not checkpoint-only I/O

runtime.scope: observed Tokio scheduler worker pool size; not busy or physical thread count; per-client I/O depth and workload unchanged
